inspiration.display: ecology / niche partitioning + statistics + scheduling theory

why_interesting: The problem's 'Runtime Adaptation' dimension (how the system changes its own behaviour while running) is where the conventional approach carries a structural assumption: Design-time parameters are tuned for an average case, so the system is rarely at its best for the case actually running. AARL took a mechanism that already works in ecology / niche partitioning, statistics, scheduling theory - Treat non-uniform participants as exploitable structure instead of averaging them away. - and asked what happens if it is applied to GPU. If the mechanism transfers, the gain would come from removing that assumption rather than from tuning the existing design. Whether it transfers is exactly what is not established here.

first_experiment.objective: Establish whether the mechanism moves stability of achieved performance for GPU at all, before tuning anything.
first_experiment.design: Baseline A: the conventional runtime adaptation approach. Variant B: the Heterogeneity awareness mechanism applied only to the runtime adaptation dimension. Keep every other parameter identical and use the same seed/warm-up.
first_experiment.decision_rule: Only claim support if B moves stability of achieved performance outside the run-to-run spread of A; if the spread is larger than the effect, report INCONCLUSIVE rather than a direction.
first_experiment.what_would_make_it_stop: If A is already at the physical or structural limit of stability of achieved performance, the comparison cannot discriminate and the design must change.
